To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3B43 RT is a suitable near real time SPPP for flood simulation, and IMERG Final is a suitable post real time SPPP, for the study area.

IMERG F is a suitable replacement for 3B42 V7 for flood simulation at 3 hourly temporal scales in the study area, and the GPM era IMERGE F is more accurate than its predecessor 3B42v7, indicating that the GPM era SPSs can be used to replace the TRMM era SPPs for flood simulation in the study area.
IMERG F is a reliable alternative for the TRMM era SPPs in the study area and that the GPM era IMERGE F SPP is the most suitable SPP for flood simulation and flood prediction in the study area.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evaluation of the GPM era SPSs in both near and post real time versions for flood simulation at sub daily scales in a poorly gaged watershed in Myanmar, and the study provides a reference for the hydrological community in sparsely or ungaug ed basins to select suitable precipitation data sources.

the evaluation of GPM era SPSs for hydrological applications, and the proposed framework can serve as a reference to hydrologists and water resources managers for hydrological assessment of SPSs in poorly gauged watersheds in other parts of the world.

the hydrological application of SPPs in poorly gauged basins, and it provides useful information for the scientific community to better understand the utility of SPPs for flood simulation in poorly gauging basins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GPM era SPSs are still not ready to replace gauge data for flood simulations at sub daily scales in poorly gauged or even ungauged watersheds.
GPM era SPSs are generally reliable and accurate for hydrological applications, and the GPM scientific community has to improve the quality of SPPs for ungauged and sparsely gauges basins.

GPM era SPSs, especially IMERG F and IMERG L, are reliable and accurate enough for hydrological applications, and they are the promising candidates to replace the TRMM era 2B42V7 SPS in poorly gauged basins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TRMM and GMP era SPPs are promising for flood simulation and flood prediction in poorly gauged or even ungauged areas in Myanmar.
the GPM era SPSs are reliable for flood simulations at sub daily scales in the study basin, and 3B43RT and IMERG F are recommended for near and post real time flood simulations, respectively.

IMERG F, IMERG E, and GSMaPs can be used as alternative precipitation data sources for flood simulation at 3 hourly time scales, and IMERG E and GSMaP NTR can be used for 3 hourly flood forecasting in the study area, but IMERG L and GSMaP MV and GSMaP G are not reliable for flood simulation and forecasting at 3 hourly scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3B4 2RT and IMERG F are reliable SPPs that can be used to estimate precipitation in poorly gauged basins at sub daily temporal resolution, which is critical in flood prediction.
the GPM SPPs can be used as an alternative source of precipitation data for flood simulations in poorly gauged watersheds.

3 hourly SPPs, such as 3B42 RT, IMERG F, and IMERG E, are more suitable for flood simulation in the study area than the daily SPPs, including 3B42 V7 and GSMaP MV, due to their higher temporal resolutions.
